newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish hot dog stall wins McDonald's court fight.
newsitem.headline: Danish hot dog stall wins McDonald's court fight.

text.p: Hot-dog seller Allan Pedersen won a 30-month court fight against McDonald's Corp on Wednesday, when the Danish supreme court rejected the U.S. fast food giant's claim that his McAllan roadside stand infringed its copyright.
McDonald's said it was the first time it had lost a case concerning a food business.
Pedersen, whose trailer in the provincial town of Silkeborg was named after Scotch whisky distiller Macallan, said he would celebrate his win with a visit to Scotland.

"I have a standing invitation from Macallan in Scotland to go and visit them. They have never sold so much whisky in Denmark as they have since my case started, two and a half years ago," he told a news conference.
McDonald's Danish management said the judgement, in which it was ordered to pay 40,000 crowns in costs, opened the floodgates to imitators.

"The general rule in trademark cases is that there should be a risk of confusion, which there is not in this case. Nobody would think that they are at a McDonald's because this hot dog stand is called McAllan," he told the Danish news agency Ritzau. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33 969650
